# Greenware

> Greenware is a source language for 3D assets. One `.gw` file describes one asset, such as a prop, a building, a vehicle or a character. The compiler turns the file into a glTF 2.0 binary (GLB) with the same bytes on every run, and it checks the file. Greenware is pre-1.0: the language, the compiler and the file format change without notice.

Source: https://github.com/odvcencio/greenware

The README says much of the language is still unbuilt. `CHANGELOG.md` lists what works now.

## Start here

- [Examples](examples/): the goal post, helmet, rigged arm (`examples/arm`) and athlete.
- [Goal post source](examples/goalpost/goalpost.gw): the example to start from. It uses parameters, materials, parts, sockets, levels of detail, collision, a budget and outputs.
- [Goal post acceptance tests](examples/goalpost/goalpost.accept.gw): the checks that run on the decoded GLB files of the goal post at each level of detail.
- [Overview](README.md): a short example, the layout and the licence.
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): what changed and what works now.

## Commands

- [Command-line tool](cmd/greenware/main.go): the commands are `build <file>` (writes GLB files), `check <file>` (lists diagnostics), `fmt <file>` (formats source), `accept <source.gw> <accept.gw> --glb-dir DIR` (runs acceptance tests), `print <file>` (writes a 3MF file), and the authoring commands `fix`, `diff`, `describe`, `ir`, `init`, `lock`, `explain`, `search` and `trace`. Each command takes `--json`.
- [Command reference](docs/reference/commands.md): every command, its flags and its exit status.
- [Printing](docs/reference/print.md): the 3MF backend and the `GW-PRINT` gate.
- Exit status: 0 means success. 1 means an error diagnostic, or a file that `fmt --check` finds unformatted. 2 means a usage or read error. `accept` exits 3 when no check failed but some could not be measured.

## Code map

- [lang/](lang/): parses and formats `.gw` files. Holds the parser blob `greenware.bin`.
- [language/](language/): the names that identify the language, and the grammar source in `language/grammar`.
- [ast/](ast/): the typed declaration model. Lowers a parsed tree into a file.
- [resolve/](resolve/): binds names, orders `let` declarations and evaluates constants.
- [units/](units/): values, dimensions and arithmetic. Lengths are metres and angles are radians.
- [registry/](registry/): the fields, child blocks and rows that each declaration accepts.
- [diag/](diag/): diagnostics, with their codes and severities.
- [compiler/](compiler/): the back end. Builds each output into GLB files or a 3MF print, and reserves cost tickets.
- [std/](std/): the standard library of `.gw` sources.
- [tools/](tools/): the authoring commands (`fix`, `diff`, `describe`, `ir`, `init`, `lock`, `explain`, `search`, `trace`).
- [backend/threemf/](backend/threemf/): the 3MF writer, reader and validator.
- [accept/](accept/): runs acceptance files on decoded GLB files.
- [kernel/](kernel/): the geometry kernel. `kernel/build` makes parametric shapes, `kernel/mesh` holds the mesh type, `kernel/geom` measures distance, `kernel/image` makes textures and `kernel/rig` compiles skeletons, skins, morphs and clips.
- [gltf/](gltf/): reads and writes GLB. Its own module, and it imports only `det`.
- [det/](det/): deterministic scalar math. Its own module.
- [conformance/](conformance/): an independent checker in its own module. It reads no Greenware code.

## Reference

- [Diagnostic codes](diag/catalogue.go): the one list of codes. Each entry gives a code, its severity, when it is reported and a fixture that triggers it.
- [Grammar reference](docs/reference/grammar.ebnf): the generated EBNF grammar.
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): how to build, test and change the project.
- [Agent rules](AGENTS.md): the rules for automated and human contributors.
- [Licence](LICENSE): MIT, copyright M31 Labs.
